skill.name: web-search-scraper-api-skill
skill.description: Extract Markdown from web pages using the BrowserAct Web Search Scraper API. The skill runs a Python wrapper that submits one target URL, polls the task, and prints the returned content.
skill.summary: Extract webpage content as Markdown through the BrowserAct API.
skill.author: browser-act

security_audit.summary: The skill intentionally makes authenticated HTTPS requests to BrowserAct and reads only BROWSERACT_API_KEY from the environment. Most generic secret and Markdown backtick matches are false positives, but the guidance asking users to provide an API key directly is a real credential exposure risk.

remediation.suggestion: Remove instructions that ask users to provide API keys in chat. Require environment variables or a secure secret manager instead.
State clearly that target URLs and resulting task data are sent to BrowserAct for processing.
Validate that inputs are HTTP or HTTPS URLs and advise users to process only authorized public pages.

content.value_statement: Manual page copying is slow and often loses structure. This skill sends a target URL to BrowserAct and returns clean Markdown for research or documentation work.
actual_capabilities: Accepts one target URL as the script argument.
Uses BROWSERACT_API_KEY from the environment for authentication.
Starts a BrowserAct workflow task for the target URL.
Polls task status until completion, failure, or timeout.
Prints returned Markdown or the API response content to the terminal.
limitations: Requires Python, the requests package, and a valid BrowserAct API key.
Sends the target URL and task data to BrowserAct.
Processes one URL per script invocation.
May wait up to five minutes before timing out.

use_cases.title: Article Research
use_cases.description: Extract a public article into Markdown for review, notes, or citation planning.

use_cases.title: Documentation Capture
use_cases.description: Convert a documentation page into structured Markdown for offline study or migration.

use_cases.title: Content Review
use_cases.description: Capture public page text so teams can compare updates and preserve source context.

prompt_templates.title: Extract One Page
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract Markdown from this public URL: https://example.com/article. Show the returned content after the task completes.

prompt_templates.title: Convert Documentation
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this documentation page to Markdown and keep the original heading order: https://example.com/docs/page.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Public Pages
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract these two approved public URLs one at a time, then list the main content differences in plain language.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Research Notes
prompt_templates.prompt: Extract Markdown from these approved source URLs one at a time. Return concise notes with source titles and important sections.

output_examples.input: Extract the content from a public product blog post.
output_examples.output: A Markdown article with title, headings, links, and paragraph text ready for review.

output_examples.input: Capture a documentation page for offline notes.
output: Any API error message shown plainly

output_examples.input: Review a public webpage for updated content.
output_examples.output: A readable Markdown version of the page that can be compared with earlier notes.

best_practices: Store BROWSERACT_API_KEY in the environment or a secret manager.
Use public URLs or pages you have permission to process.
Review extracted Markdown before using it as authoritative source material.
anti_patterns: Do not paste API keys into prompts, chat messages, or shared logs.
Do not scrape private, paid, or sensitive pages without authorization.
Do not assume empty or partial output means the page has no content.

faq.question: Does this run locally?
faq.answer: The wrapper runs locally, but extraction is performed by the BrowserAct API.

faq.question: Does it need an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires BROWSERACT_API_KEY before it can start a BrowserAct workflow.

faq.question: Can it handle any URL?
faq.answer: It accepts HTTP and HTTPS URLs, but access depends on BrowserAct and the target site.

faq.question: Where does the output appear?
faq.answer: The script prints status messages and final Markdown in the terminal.

faq.question: Can I process multiple pages?
faq.answer: Yes, but the bundled script processes one URL per invocation.

faq.question: Is it safe for secrets?
faq.answer: Use environment variables. Do not paste API keys or sensitive page content into shared chats.
